title: Event-Grounded Sparse Autoencoders for Vision-Language-Action Policies
claim: A multi-stage procedure turns model activations into behavior-grounded features and validates them causally through targeted latent interventions.
layout: 4 numbered panels in 2x2 grid, color-coded borders, left-to-right flow
description: A 2x2 grid of rounded, color-bordered panels, each numbered with a colored circle. Panel 1 (orange) shows a VLA transformer backbone feeding hidden states h into a sparse autoencoder. The SAE is drawn as W_enc, BatchTopK, sparse latent z and W_dec, followed by the reconstruction-plus-auxiliary loss. Panel 2 (green) plots a 3D end-effector trajectory as a blue curve with green circles marking keyframes. Panel 3 (purple) shows robot image strips from four tasks. The strips are clustered into colored dot clouds, and a VLM annotates each cluster with phase and phrase labels. Panel 4 (red) shows latent z being edited to z′ using candidate SAE features. It compares baseline and intervention rollouts as image strips, with a check mark for the baseline and an X for the intervention, and gives the edit equation h′ = h + Dec(z′) − Dec(z). The eye goes first to the colorful numbered headers.
caption: This figure shows the 4 stages of the event-grounded SAE pipeline: (1) SAE training (Sec. [ref]); (2) kinematic keyframe extraction (Sec. [ref]); (3) task-local event clustering with VLM annotation (Sec. [ref]); (4) closed-loop validation through residual-preserving latent edits (Sec. [ref]).
abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies translate language and visual inputs into robot actions, where their hidden representations directly shape closed-loop behavior. However, mechanistic interpretability tools from language and vision-language models do not transfer cleanly to VLAs: outputs are robot actions rather than human-readable tokens, and validating internal changes requires expensive closed-loop rollouts. We propose an event-grounded interpretability pipeline that anchors SAE feature analysis to behavioral events rather than text contexts. We extract keyframes from end-effector trajectories and cluster them within each task using visual, robot-state, and temporal cues. The resulting events guide SAE feature ranking, with optional VLM annotations providing descriptions of the events. To our knowledge, our pipeline is among the first to ground SAE-based VLA analysis in closed-loop behavioral events. Across two simulation architectures and a real-robot study, event-grounded ranking yields the strongest causal effects on OpenVLA and transfers to the continuous action chunks of $Ï_{0.5}$. SAE is a sparse but imperfect intervention basis: usability varies with architecture and intervention site, and aggressive intervention reveals safety and interpretability limits. Overall, event-grounded SAE analysis emerges as a practical starting point for behavior-anchored VLA interpretability, motivating future work on SAE analysis beyond end-effector motion, finer-grained closed-loop evaluation, and safe interventions for high-stakes VLA deployments.
